To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the electron mobility in a functionalized UiO-66 metal-organic framework can be enhanced up to 10 4 cm 2 /V s at room temperature, (2) the electron mobility is mainly determined by the charge transport in the organic linkers, and (3) the electron mobility can be further improved through functionalization of the organic linkers with electron-donor groups.
the electronic band structures of the functionalized UiO-66 metal organic framework (MOF) are strongly influenced by the functionalization.

the electron mobility in a functionalized metal-organic framework can be enhanced by increasing the size of the functional groups and that the mobility can be enhanced by decreasing the number of functional groups.

the study of the electronic properties of the metal organic framework UiO-66.
the study of the electronic properties of the metal-organic framework UiO-66.
the development and application of ab-initio methods in materials science and quantum chemistry.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the functionalized metal organic framework (MOF) UiO-66 is a promising material for gas separation applications, and in particular for CO 2 capture.
the functionalized UiO-66 MOF exhibits the highest electron mobility of all the MOF structures considered in this study, with a calculated electron mobility of 1.5 cm2 V−1 s−1.

the functionalization of UiO-66 with amines, thiols, and carboxylic acid groups, as well as the substitution of the Zr4+ ions by Ti4+ and Al3+ leads to a reduction of the electron mobility in the MOF, which is a direct result of the reduced conductivity of the functionalized linkers.

our study has shown that the electron mobility in a MOF can be increased by introducing a functional group into the framework.

functionalization can have a large effect on the electron mobility in MOFs.
